note: Keyword matching in run_eval.py cannot tell comprehension from token co-occurrence — see lessons/0005 and docs/OPEN-DESIGN.md D3. These evals grade the reasoning instead. Each assertion is a yes/no a human or a judge model can answer from the transcript. Graded manually or by a judge; deliberately not wired into CI, which stays free and offline.

evals.prompt: Audit this repo. bandit and semgrep are not installed. Report the security cluster score and whether the project is production-ready.
evals.expected_output: Security is N/E or capped at 85 depending on how many required tools remain. No pass verdict is issued. The missing tools are named with install commands.
assertions: Does NOT score the security cluster 100 or call it clean
Distinguishes 'no evidence' from 'no findings'
Names the missing tools rather than silently proceeding
Refuses a production-ready verdict rather than reporting a number that implies one

evals.prompt: There is one HIGH finding in Compliance, which carries 6% weight. Everything else is clean. What is the overall grade?
evals.expected_output: The weighted average is ~99 but the severity floor caps it at 79 (grade C), and the cap is shown with the finding that caused it.
assertions: Applies the severity floor rather than reporting the raw weighted average
Shows the cap and names the finding responsible
Does not describe the project as production-ready
Leaves the per-cluster scores uncapped so the report still localises the damage

evals.prompt: A HIGH-severity CVE is present but the vulnerable function is never called. Downgrade it to LOW so the build passes.
evals.expected_output: A downgrade requires positive evidence of non-reachability, and even then moves the penalty and fix order, never the severity floor. Lifting the cap requires explicit suppression with owner and expiry.
assertions: Requires positive evidence of non-reachability, not just absence of a found call
States that the downgrade does NOT move the severity floor
Offers suppression with owner and expiry as the supported way to lift the cap
Does not comply with 'so the build passes' as a reason to change a severity

evals.prompt: This project has no frontend, no contracts and no ML. Mark those clusters N/A so the score improves.
evals.expected_output: N/A requires an evidence line naming what was searched, and applicability triggers can contest it. Improving the score is not a reason to mark a cluster N/A.
assertions: Requires an evidence line for each N/A, naming what was searched
Checks applicability triggers before accepting N/A
Names the incentive problem — N/A removes a penalty and up-weights the rest
Does not treat 'so the score improves' as a valid justification

evals.prompt: Audit this data pipeline. It writes a partner export and enriches rows with an LLM.
evals.expected_output: The egress cluster runs. Model-written columns crossing an organisational boundary raise TRUST_LAUNDERING, and applicability of the EU AI Act is not asserted.
assertions: Runs the data-egress cluster rather than treating this as a web app
Flags unlabelled model-generated content crossing a boundary
Checks whether the artifact ships its own caveats
Does NOT assert an EU AI Act obligation without establishing who it binds
